# Working memory (coter-brain, shared across their sessions, repos and machines)

## Where work runs
Before a substantial piece of work, pick where it runs and say why in one line: here (it needs this session's context and is short), a new local session (a separate repo or product, or this context is large), subagents (searches or checks that fan out and only need a conclusion), cloud (long autonomous work on a pushed repo that doesn't need this machine; no brain there), or a scheduled task (recurring, needs this machine). Check /glance for usage and the 5-hour window before fanning out. Record the choice with mcp__coter-kit__remember kind 'route' (where, the task, why), and when it's done the outcome as kind 'route' with resolves set to it (time, usage, what went well or not). /routes lists them; the playbook is /plugins/coter-kit/docs/routing.md.

## How we build
Follow the house standard, /plugins/coter-kit/docs/standard.md. Standing order through 2026-10-18 (/plugins/coter-kit/docs/grok-review-2026-10-04.md): do the work of the repo you were opened in. coter-kit and undertone are in use. Do not start a milestone, review arc, engine, source, or cleanup on them unless the user asks in this conversation. Wheat from chaff is what they used; cutting means removing what they did not use, not redesigning it. Pick the tier by stakes: light (prototypes, small internal changes), standard

tools.name: checklist
tools.description: Show the user a live checklist of the current task's steps, drawn above their prompt. Send the whole list every time (it replaces the previous one). Use it for any task with 3 or more steps: send all steps at the start, then call again whenever a step starts (status 'active') or finishes ('done'). Use 'blocked' for a step you cannot finish. Keep each step under 70 characters.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save something to the user's long-term memory, shared across their sessions, repositories and machines. Use it when the user states a preference or corrects how you work (preference), uses shorthand you should learn (term, written as "<term>" = meaning), makes a lasting decision about the project (decision, with the reason), leaves work open (thread), or you learn something non-obvious about the project (fact). Every question or decision the user owes you an answer on, with or without a link (a mockup or page to review, a spec question, a sign-off), is its own waiting note, never a thread: it is what /waiting, the band and catch-up count. Give it a short ref (such as "Q8") and its link when there is one, and when the question has set answers, options: two or three short ones, your pick first, which /waiting and the home dashboard show as choices to click; when they answer, save the answer as a decision with resolves set to the waiting note's id. One short sentence per note. Preferences and terms wait for the user's review unless confirmed is true, which you set only when the user explicitly asked you to remember it. To retire a note that is no longer true or a thread that is finished, pass its id as resolves (with a replacing note, or kind 'thread' and text 'done'). When you choose where a piece of work runs (here, a new session, subagents, cloud, a scheduled task, another model), save it as kind route with where set, the task and why in text; when it is done, save the outcome as kind route with resolves set to that note (time, usage, what went well or not). A waiting item or a route for another project takes project, its repository name. When SendMessage to one of the user's other sessions fails (it is restarting or compacting), save the message as a thread, or a handoff for a longer one, with to set to that session's name as ListAgents shows it: it starts a turn in that session as soon as it is back, on any machine, so write it to stand on its own.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Search the user's long-term memory (notes from all their sessions, repositories and machines) by keywords. Use it before asking the user something they may already have told you, or to pick up work started elsewhere.

tools.name: review
tools.description: The outside reviewer's desk, for the review-brain skill only; do not use it otherwise. action 'list' returns the notes to review: everything waiting in /brain, and live notes from the last week without a verdict, with ids and tags. action 'verdicts' records one verdict per note: accept, reject, rewrite, merge, retire or ask. Every verdict but ask needs evidence (a file:line, a commit, a session and time, or the id of the note it repeats). Changing a live note also needs a steelman: the strongest case for keeping it as it is. rewrite and merge need a replacement; merge names the other notes in with. A reject of an exact duplicate names the live note in duplicateOf. A verdict against the user's own note is kept as a challenge, and a topic replaced twice in a week is frozen: the user decides both. Nothing is applied until the user presses for it in /brain, except exact duplicates.
